text:
alex cheng: Heads-up — I'm working on migrating the 'hello-serverless' quickstart to the SDK v8 auth flow + a tiny container deploy section. I pushed a draft PR but the auth snippet is failing when I run the example locally. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3421

jess rao: Link looks good. What's failing locally? paste the error?

alex cheng: error is a 401 from the API. Locally I'm using the old REDWOOD_TOKEN var pattern from the v6 docs. The SDK v8 expects the client to read from REDWOOD_API_KEY and the example helper changed names.

li wang: ah yep we renamed the helper to createClientFromEnv. In the new quickstart we should show both (minimal) env var + Node snippet. Suggestion: show export + example that uses the helper.

maria gonzalez: Can you add a tiny note about KMS customers who use instance roles? We had a support case where people missed the KMS hint and got confused. Maybe a one-liner under "Auth" pointing to enterprise KMS docs.

alex cheng: good call, will add. Also the container deploy step lost the --build-arg in the Dockerfile example when we collapsed files. Need to restore it so people can pass in the API key at build time if they choose.

jess rao: For the PR: assign @li and @maria as reviewers. Also open a follow-up issue to add a short automated smoke test in CI that runs the hello-serverless example (no real tokens, just lint + build).

alex cheng: done — added reviewers and a TODO in the PR description: "add CI smoke test". Pushed a new commit with env var rename and the helper call update.

docs-bot: CI check started for PR #3421 — lint, linkcheck, mdspell.

ci-bot: linkcheck: warning: broken link in docs/quickstart/hello-serverless.md line 42 -> https://old-link.example/auth-info (redirected).

alex cheng: thanks CI. I'll fix the link to point to /enterprise/kms or the new auth guide.

li wang: Quick snippet to include (Node):
```js
import { createClientFromEnv } from '@redwood/inference-sdk';
const client = createClientFromEnv();
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-v1', prompt: 'hi' });
console.log(res.text);
```

jess rao: Nice. Keep it minimal. Also add a short Python snippet variant.

alex cheng: added both snippets and a small code block for exporting envs:
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"<YOUR_KEY>\"
# optional for KMS users: export REDWOOD_KMS_KEY=\"projects/...\"
```

maria gonzalez: lgtm for content. Two nits: 1) callout that users should never commit keys to Docker images, and 2) link to our secret management docs.

alex cheng: added both nits and a short admonition in the container section: "prefer runtime injection or build-time ARGs that don't land in final image layers" with link to secrets doc.

li wang: I left an inline suggestion in the PR to keep the API example to <=6 lines and to remove an extra explanatory paragraph that duplicates the SDK README.

alex cheng: addressed suggestion, squashed commits, and pushed.

jess rao: will review in the morning. If nothing major, can we merge and cut a tiny patch release to the site?

maria gonzalez: yes please. We should also backport the link fix to the older quickstarts (hello-embed, hello-chat).

alex cheng: opening a follow-up PR for backports after merge. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

docs-bot: PR #3421 merged by jess rao — site redeploy scheduled.

ci-bot: deploy: started — staging build 2026-03-23T08:15:00Z

alex cheng: verified staging render, auth snippet works with env var, container note is present. I'll watch production deploy.

jess rao: amazing, great catch on the env var rename. small win for onboarding.

maria gonzalez: closing thread — will file the CI smoke test issue this week and add the KMS example to enterprise docs.
